content: 1. Combined exposure to abrocitinib and its active metabolites may lead to a loss or reduction in clinical response. 2. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers. If unavoidable, increase the acalabrutinib dose to 200 mg twice daily. 3. Rifampin reduces acetaminophen levels by enhancing its metabolism, potentially increasing hepatotoxic metabolite levels. This applies to oral, IV, and rectal forms. The clinical significance is unknown. 4. Rifampin decreases adagrasib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Rifampin reduces afatinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If chronic therapy with a P-gp inducer is required, increase the afatinib dose by 10 mg daily as tolerated, and resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the inducer. 6. Rifampin decreases alfentanil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Rifampin reduces aliskiren levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. 8. Rifampin decreases almotriptan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Rifampin reduces alosetron levels by inducing CYP1A2, CYP3A4, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Rifampin decreases alpelisib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 11. Rifampin reduces alprazolam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Aluminum hydroxide reduces rifampin absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 13. Rifampin decreases ambrisentan levels by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 14. Rifampin reduces amikacin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Rifampin decreases amiodarone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Rifampin reduces amitriptyline levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Rifampin decreases amlodipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Rifampin reduces amobarbital levels by enhancing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Rifampin decreases ampicillin levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 20. Rifampin reduces antipyrine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Apalutamide decreases rifampin levels by increasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Rifampin reduces apixaban levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Rifampin decreases apremilast levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing efficacy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Rifampin reduces aprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Rifampin decreases aripiprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Rifampin reduces armodafinil levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Rifampin decreases artemether/lumefantrine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing antimalarial efficacy. Coadministration is contraindicated. 28. Rifampin reduces artesunate levels by inducing UGT metabolism, potentially decreasing active metabolite (DHA) levels. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 29. Rifampin decreases asenapine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Rifampin reduces atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 31. Rifampin decreases atogepant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Rifampin reduces atorvastatin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Rifampin decreases atovaquone levels by enhancing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Rifampin reduces avanafil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor response carefully in patients with erectile dysfunction. 35. Rifampin decreases avapritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Rifampin reduces avatrombopag levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the starting dose when treating ITP with moderate or strong CYP2C9/3A4 inducers. 37. Rifampin decreases axitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Azithromycin increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Rifampin reduces bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Rifampin decreases BCG vaccine live levels due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 41. Rifampin reduces bedaquiline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 42. Rifampin decreases belumosudil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the belumosudil dose to 200 mg PO BID when coadministered with strong CYP3A inducers. 43. Rifampin reduces bendamustine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Bentonite decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. 45. Rifampin reduces benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers, as hydrocodone plasma concentrations may increase, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 46. Rifampin decreases berotralstat levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor or titrate P-gp substrate dose if coadministered. 47. Rifampin reduces bexagliflozin levels by inducing UGT1A9 metabolism. Consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent for additional glycemic control. 48. Rifampin decreases bexarotene levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Rifampin reduces bictegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 metabolism, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Coadministration is contraindicated. 50. Rifampin decreases bisoprolol levels by enhancing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 51. Rifampin reduces bortezomib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Rifampin decreases bosentan levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Bosutinib increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Rifampin decreases bosutinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Rifampin reduces brentuximab vedotin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Rifampin decreases brexpiprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Double the brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks if coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. 56. Rifampin reduces brigatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Rifampin decreases brivaracetam levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
